Hi Laura,

We are in the final stages of our annual vendor recertification and Redwood's SOC2 attestation is on our checklist. Separately, our usage has grown faster than forecasted — we are considering a capacity uplift of ~20% for Q4 and would like to combine that with the renewal amendment if possible. Is there a straightforward path to bundle the retention change + seat/bandwidth top-up into one amendment and a single procurement flow?

Can you share a recommended evidence handoff protocol and a draft amendment we can circulate internally (procurement and legal)? Our procurement lead, Tom Wu, is on copy and would like visibility into timing for DocuSign.

Thanks — Alicia

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks for the note — happy to coordinate. Short answers up front: yes, we can combine the retention change and the 20% capacity uplift into a single amendment and a single DocuSign flow; and yes, we have an evidence routing pattern we recommend for large audits.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): Redwood provides evidence index + sample logs (see attached evidence_index_v3.xlsx) and a draft amendment for review.
- Week 1: TileBank security reviews artifacts and confirms retention horizon (we've left options for 365 / 545 in the draft).
- Week 2: Procurement (Tom) reviews amendment; e-signature via DocuSign.
- Week 3: Bulk evidence handoff (SFTP / secure Share) and completion of attestation questionnaire.

Evidence routing details: for a set this size we suggest a two-stage delivery — (A) metadata index + small sample logs over Share link for early review, (B) bulk transfer via encrypted SFTP or signed presigned manifests. We will produce a checksum manifest and a parallel audit log sample bundle (sample_audit_logs_202805.tar.gz). Our security/compliance team will manage endpoint credentials and rotation window.

I'll loop in Ben from Finance to confirm pricing for the +20% capacity uplift and include language options in the amendment. Marissa (CS) will run execution on the evidence transfer and scheduling.

Attached: evidence_index_v3.xlsx (index), draft amendment placeholder (amendment_draft_tilebank_20280909.pdf).

If that timeline works, I'll send the DocuSign-ready amendment by Monday.

Best,

Subject: Internal: pricing language and DocuSign prep for DL-4830

Folks — looping in the pricing/finance note for the TileBank amendment (deal_id DL-4830). I drafted two options to include in the amendment:

Option A (one-time top-up): +20% capacity (seat/bandwidth) for remainder of contract term, one-time prorated charge.
Option B (recurring uplift): +20% committed baseline going forward with monthly billing at the committed rate (requires minimum 6-month commitment).

Suggested contract language snippet (concise): 
"Seller will increase the Customer's committed capacity by twenty percent (20%) effective on execution. Charges for the increased capacity shall be pro-rated for the billing cycle during which the increase is executed unless Option B is selected, in which case the committed baseline will reflect the higher capacity at the next billing period."

For retention we should include a single explicit selection field in the DocuSign page: 365 days OR 545 days. Procurement can initial the chosen line.

I'll prepare a DocuSign package with two checkboxes (Capacity Option A/B, Retention: 365/545) and an instructions page. Marissa — once I hand off the package can you coordinate the evidence handoff schedule? Ben — can you confirm the prorated amount for Option A and the delta for Option B and post back by EOD Tuesday?

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Commercial Operations
